To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of MART1 is not detected in the peripheral blood of vitiligo patient but is present in the peripheral blood from healthy individuals.
MART1 transcripts are absent in the PBMC of Vitiligo patients but are detected in healthy controls.
1) MART-1 transcript is not detected in PBMCs obtained from Vitiligo (VI) patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that are not expressed in PBMCs in vitiligo, which can be used as biomarkers in the future.
the identification of genes that are not expressed in PBMCs in vitiligo and may be responsible for induction of autoimmunitiy in vitiligo.
the identification of the mechanism responsible for the breakdown of tolerance in vitiliginous skin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nonexpression of these antigens in PBMCs is the cause of breakdown of tolerance and induction of autoimmunuity.
the absence of MART1 and TRP-2 transcripts in PBMCs is a result of the loss of tolerance against these proteins in vitiligo.
MART-1 is not expressed at the transcriptional level in PBMCs in Vitiligo patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absence of TRP-2 and MART-1 in PBMC of vitiligo patient is due to a failure to express these antigens in the periphery, and not due to a thymic defect.

in vitiligo, the absence of self-antigens (TRP-1 and TRP-2) in the periphery results in loss of peripheral tolerance and the absence of self antigen (MART-1) in the periphary results in loss of central tolerance.
the absence of TRP-2 and MART-1 transcripts in PBMCs is the cause for the induction of autoantibody production in vitiligo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the lack of MART1 transcripts in the PBMC of vitiligo patient can lead to the breakdown of peripheral tolerance towards MART1 and finally results in the induction of autoimmune response against MART1.
MART-1 is a self antigen which is absent in the PBMC of vitiligo and therefore may play a role in the pathogenesis of vitiligo.
the non-expression of these antigens in PBMCs is a result of the breakdown of peripheral tolerance and not the cause of the disease.
